planned_probe.constant_config: same as accepted demo_current_sota config: vendor, native GGUF, cpu_moe=40, vram_cache=0, one-prefill limit=3000, gate pack O_DIRECT, keep-topk 4 with layers 10-39=>3, strict drop_caches, MemoryMax=16000000000, MemorySwapMax=0
planned_probe.correctness_gate: France output must be semantic/coherent and runner correctness_ok=true.
planned_probe.promotion_gate: If eval_tok_s > 4.4 with TTFT/RAM/correctness passing, immediately run a clean reproduction before accepting and push all source/artifacts. If not, record rejected and do not repeat sampling.

purpose: Plan a bounded no-source OpenMP wait-policy probe on the accepted SOTA route.

theory.upper_bound: Treat as a SOTA-polish probe only. It can be promoted only if strict cold eval_tok_s > 4.4, correctness passes, RAM/page-cache stays within 16GB, and TTFT <= 33617.688744 ms. It does not reopen the 10 tok/s route unless the measured improvement is unexpectedly large and reproducible.
theory.why_it_cannot_be_10tok_path: The current post-TTFT generation window is about 31.262 s for roughly 137.6 generated tokens. Reaching 10 tok/s for the same output would require saving about 17.507 s. The CPU chunk critical path is about 27 s and is dominated by exact up/down work and memory traffic; wait-policy tuning can only reduce scheduling/wakeup overhead, not remove the exact fallback payload.
theory.why_it_might_help: ggml is built with libgomp and uses an OpenMP parallel region for graph compute. CPU up/down fallback dominates decode, so worker sleep/wakeup policy might affect per-token scheduling latency without changing model math.
